title: Experimental studies of the short-term physical loads and stresses experienced by women when pulling and pushing a wheelchair under various working conditions.
summary: Pulling and pushing wheelchairs is a typical and common form of physical work in a nursing context. This type of physical strain occurs frequently in day-to-day work, both in inpatient and outpatient care. Prolonged, intensive physical work can lead to overexertion and increased strain on various parts of the body. This raises the question of what level of physical exertion and strain is permissible when pulling and pushing wheelchairs under various conditions, such as varying surface types, steep ramp gradients or different patient weights. To date, there is very little data that objectively describes this issue. We are therefore conducting experimental studies into short-term physical strain and stress when pulling and pushing wheelchairs. The long-term aim is to draw validated conclusions about the intense physical strain and stress involved in pulling and pushing wheelchairs and to provide recommendations on how to reduce strain-related overexertion and the resulting musculoskeletal disorders.
conditions: Only healthy women who have undergone a medical examination will be included.

interventions.name: Prospective analysis of all female participants with regard to biomechanical parameters whilst pulling and pushing a wheelchair along a test track.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Appears healthy based on medical history and clinical examination.
Exclusion criteria:
Failed the initial medical examination.
